import numpy as np
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.circuit import Parameter
from qiskit.circuit.library import PauliEvolutionGate
from qiskit.quantum_info import SparsePauliOp, Statevector

t = Parameter("t")
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.append(PauliEvolutionGate(SparsePauliOp("XX"), time=t), [0, 1])

bound = qc.assign_parameters({t: np.pi / 6})
print(Statevector(bound).probabilities_dict())

explanation.correct: `PauliEvolutionGate(H, time=t)` implements exp(−i·t·H) — no factor ½. Because (X⊗X)² = I, exp(−i t XX) = cos t·I − i sin t·XX, which maps |00⟩ to cos t|00⟩ − i sin t|11⟩. With t bound to π/6: P(00) = cos²(π/6) = 0.75 and P(11) = sin²(π/6) = 0.25. XX flips both qubits together, so |01⟩ and |10⟩ never appear.

distractors.A: This uses the rotation-gate convention exp(−i t/2 XX) (that is `RXXGate(t)`). `PauliEvolutionGate` has no ½: its time multiplies the operator directly.
distractors.B: This doubles the exponent to exp(−i 2t XX), as if the bound value were a rotation angle to be doubled; it swaps the two probabilities.
distractors.C: This treats XX as two independent X rotations, one per qubit. exp(−i t X⊗X) is a joint rotation that only couples |00⟩ with |11⟩.

from qiskit.circuit import Parameter
from qiskit.circuit.library import PauliEvolutionGate, RXXGate
from qiskit.quantum_info import SparsePauliOp, Statevector


def probs(qc):
    return {str(k): round(float(v), 4)
            for k, v in Statevector(qc).probabilities_dict().items() if float(v) > 1e-9}


t = Parameter("t")
qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
qc.append(PauliEvolutionGate(SparsePauliOp("XX"), time=t), [0, 1])
bound = qc.assign_parameters({t: np.pi / 6})
got = probs(bound)

claims = {
    "A": {"00": 0.933, "11": 0.067},
    "B": {"00": 0.25, "11": 0.75},
    "C": {"00": 0.5625, "01": 0.1875, "10": 0.1875, "11": 0.0625},
    "D": {"00": 0.75, "11": 0.25},

    evidence[k] = f"executed bound PauliEvolutionGate(XX, t=pi/6) on |00> -> {got}; option {k} claims {c} -> match={m}"
